https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body: Um Woo-chong, a veteran international administrator and former senior official at the Asian Development Bank, has been appointed the inaugural head of the World Bank Group's new accountability mechanism, making him only the second Korean to reach the vice-president level at the global institution, the Ministry of Finance and Economy said Friday. The World Bank Group’s boards of directors named Um on Wednesday as vice president and director general of the Independent Accountability Mechanism. He will take office on Jan. 18. The mechanism handles grievances from communities harmed, or at risk of being harmed, by projects the group finances, and independently reviews whether those projects meet environmental and social standards. Its chief is appointed directly by the boards and operates independently of management. The body merges three existing complaint channels — the World Bank’s Inspection Panel and Dispute Resolution Service, which is the ombudsman office serving the International Finance Corporation, along with the group’s private-sector lending arm and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, which provides political risk insurance to investors. Um has more than 30 years of experience in international development finance. He joined the Manila-based ADB in 1993 and served as its director general for sustainable development and climate change before becoming managing director general, the post coordinating key initiatives across the bank, from 2021 to 2024. He has since been CEO of the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet, a nonprofit founded in New York in 2021. His appointment follows that of Kim Sang-bu, named the World Bank’s vice president for digital and artificial intelligence in July 2024. In May, Min Jeen-ah became the group’s director of market and counterparty risk. The ministry said it expects the appointments to raise Korea’s standing in international financial institutions. It plans to keep supporting Koreans seeking such posts through recruitment briefings and programs under which the government funds young professionals to work at the institutions for two years. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.title_zh: 亚洲开发银行前官员Um Woo-chong获任世界银行集团副总裁
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body_zh: 韩国财政部周五表示，资深国际事务管理人员、亚洲开发银行前高级官员吴宇钟获任世界银行集团新问责机制首任负责人，成为第二名在該全球机构担任副总裁级别的韩国人。世界银行集团董事会周三任命吴宇钟为独立问责机制副总裁兼总干事。他将于1月18日就职。该机制负责受理受到该集团资助项目损害或可能受损社区的申诉，并独立审查这些项目是否符合环境和社会标准。其负责人由董事会直接任命，独立于管理层运作。该机构将现有三个申诉渠道合并，包括世界银行监察小组、担任国际金融公司监察专员办公室的争议解决服务，以及该集团私营部门贷款机构和提供投资者政治风险保险的多边投资担保机构。吴宇钟拥有30多年的国际发展融资经验。他于1993年加入总部位于马尼拉的亚洲开发银行，曾任可持续发展与气候变化总干事，之后于2021年至2024年担任管理总干事，负责协调该行各项重点倡议。此后，他担任全球能源联盟为人民与地球首席执行官；该非营利组织于2021年在纽约成立。他的任命紧随金相武之后，后者于2024年7月被任命为世界银行数字与人工智能副总裁。今年5月，闵贞娥出任该集团市场与交易对手风险负责人。财政部表示，预计这些任命将提升韩国在国际金融机构中的地位。该部计划通过招聘说明会和政府资助年轻专业人士到相关机构工作两年的项目，继续支持争取此类职位的韩国人。本文在生成式人工智能协助下完成，并由《韩国时报》编辑。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.summary: Seeks deliberate investment in domestic digital infrastructure, stronger regulatory institutions Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has cautioned that Nigeria should not allow a repeat of the decàdes-long mistakes it made in managing its oil economy in the burgeoning digital sector.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.summary_zh: 大力投资国内数字基础设施、强化监管机构。财政部长兼经济协调部长Taiwo Oyedele警告称，在蓬勃发展的数字经济领域，尼日利亚不应重蹈其数十年来管理石油经济时犯下的错误。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.body: Seeks deliberate investment in domestic digital infrastructure, stronger regulatory institutions Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has cautioned that Nigeria should not allow a repeat of the decàdes-long mistakes it made in managing its oil economy in the burgeoning digital sector. He recalled that exporting crude oil and importing refined petroleum products deprived Nigeria of substantial domestic value, expertise and employment opportunities, stressing that the country must not allow a similar pattern to emerge in the digital ecosystem. The minister maintained that the scale of the opportunity was already evident, citing figures by the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) showing that Nigeria had more than 157 million active internet subscriptions as at May 2026. However, he pointed out an estimate by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission showing that over 90 per cent of the country’s data is hosted abroad. The minister explained that digital sovereignty entails a country’s ability to determine, under its own laws, how its data is collected, stored, accessed and utilised, clarifying that this did not mean shutting Nigeria out of the global digital economy, but ensuring that its participation advances national interests. To reverse the trend, he called for deliberate investment in domestic digital infrastructure, stronger regulatory institutions and the development of local expertise and businesses capable of converting data into valuable products and services within Nigeria. On Artificial Intelligence (AI), Oyedele highlighted its growing capacity to reshape employment and the skills required in the emerging economy, and charged graduates to embrace AI and other emerging technologies while retaining their independent judgement, critical thinking, creativity, empathy and integrity. He also enjoined young Nigerians to be deliberate about their conduct in the digital space, noting that their online footprints increasingly influence their personal and professional identities. Their posts, comments and reactions, he noted, could shape how employers, institutions and society perceive them. The minister counselled graduates to disagree respectfully, challenge ideas rather than attack individuals, and understand that online attention does not necessarily translate into respect, popularity into credibility or virality into value creation. He also drew attention to the capacity of AI to amplify misinformation, impersonation and dishonesty, making ethical conduct and public trust increasingly important. Turning to the role of universities, Oyedele charged higher institutions to move beyond the traditional award of certificates and position themselves as centres of innovation, entrepreneurship, ethical leadership and practical problem-solving. He argued that their relevance should also be measured by the problems their graduates solve, the businesses they establish and the contributions they make to their communities. Oyedele identified agriculture, energy, healthcare, marine resources, environmental management and digital services as sectors offering significant opportunities for innovation and enterprise, calling on universities to equip students with the practical knowledge and skills to develop solutions in these areas. He outlined five responsibilities for the graduating students, including lifelong learning, value creation, integrity, responsible digital citizenship and active participation in nation-building. The minister explained that Nigeria’s digital future would depend not only on technology and infrastructure, but also on the values, choices and capabilities of the people shaping its development. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.title_zh: 奥耶德莱警告勿在数字经济领域重犯石油经济时代的错误
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.body_zh:
财政部长兼经济协调部长泰沃·奥耶德莱警告，尼日利亚不应在蓬勃发展的数字经济领域重蹈过去数十年在管理石油经济时所犯的错误。他回顾称，出口原油并进口成品油使尼日利亚损失了大量国内价值、专业知识和就业机会，强调国家必须防止类似模式在数字生态系统中出现。

这位部长表示，机会的规模已经显而易见。他援引尼日利亚通信委员会（NCC）的数据称，截至2026年5月，尼日利亚的活跃互联网订阅数已超过1.57亿。然而，他指出，尼日利亚数据保护委员会的一项估计显示，该国90%以上的数据托管在海外。

部长解释道，数字主权意味着一个国家能够依据本国法律决定其数据的收集、存储、访问和利用方式。他澄清，这并不意味着将尼日利亚排除在全球数字经济之外，而是要确保其参与全球数字经济能够推进国家利益。为扭转这一趋势，他呼吁有针对性地投资国内数字基础设施、强化监管机构，并培养本地专业人才和发展企业，使它们能够在尼日利亚国内将数据转化为有价值的产品和服务。

谈及人工智能（AI），奥耶德莱强调，人工智能日益具备重塑就业形态以及新经济所需技能的能力，并要求毕业生拥抱人工智能和其他新兴技术，同时保持独立判断力、批判性思维、创造力、同理心和正直品格。他还告诫尼日利亚年轻人，在数字空间活动时应审慎行事，因为其网络足迹正日益影响个人和职业身份。他指出，年轻人发布的帖子、评论和互动可能影响雇主、机构和社会对他们的看法。

这位部长建议毕业生以尊重的方式提出异议，对观点提出挑战而非攻击个人，并认识到网络关注度不一定会转化为尊重，人气也不一定会转化为公信力，病毒式传播更不意味着创造价值。他还提醒人们关注人工智能放大错误信息、冒名行为和不诚实现象的能力，这使得道德行为和公众信任变得日益重要。

在谈及高校的作用时，奥耶德莱要求高校超越传统颁发证书的职能，将自身定位为创新、创业、道德领导力和实际问题解决的中心。他认为，高校的相关性还应体现在其毕业生所解决的问题、所创办的企业以及对所在社区所作的贡献上。

奥耶德莱指出，农业、能源、医疗保健、海洋资源、环境管理和数字服务等领域为创新和创业提供了重大机会，并呼吁高校培养学生实用的知识和技能，使他们能够针对这些领域开发解决方案。他为即将毕业的学生提出了五项责任，包括终身学习、创造价值、保持正直、负责任地参与数字公民活动以及积极参加国家建设。

部长解释道，尼日利亚的数字未来不仅取决于技术和基础设施，也取决于塑造其发展进程的国民所秉持的价值观、所作的选择和所具备的能力。

https://leadership.ng/adc-ruling-aa-pres.summary: The AA presidential candidate, in a statement on Friday, November 6, 2026, described the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) under former Senate President David Mark and invalidating the presidential nomination of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar as troubling.
https://leadership.ng/adc-ruling-aa-pres.summary_zh: 该党总统候选人在2026年11月6日星期五发表的声明中称，联邦高等法院裁定非洲民主大会（ADC）由前参议院议长戴维·马克领导的领导层无效，并使前副总统阿提库·阿布巴卡尔的总统提名无效，此举令人不安。
https://leadership.ng/adc-ruling-aa-pres.body: He cautioned that the development could set a dangerous precedent for opposition politics, insisting that every political party and candidate had a stake in protecting democratic participation and the people’s right to choose their leaders. The AA presidential candidate, in a statement on Friday, November 6, 2026, described the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) under former Senate President David Mark and invalidating the presidential nomination of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar as troubling. He said the timing of the judgment, barely two and a half months before the 2027 general elections, had raised serious questions about judicial independence, political competition and the future of Nigeria’s democracy. Fadojoe stressed that his reaction was not based on party affiliation, noting that he was not a member of the ADC but believed that an injustice against democratic participation in one party could threaten the rights of other opposition candidates. On the role of the judiciary, Fadojoe acknowledged the importance of the courts in upholding the Constitution and ensuring that political actors operate within the law. “Why has Nigeria become a country where political parties spend more time defending their existence in courtrooms than presenting solutions to the Nigerian people?” he queried. He also questioned why elections were increasingly becoming entangled in prolonged litigation, factional disputes and last-minute judicial pronouncements. The AA presidential candidate maintained that no political party or candidate should be above the law, but insisted that judicial decisions must take into account their broader implications for democratic participation. Fadojoe consequently called for urgent measures to restore public confidence in the independence, consistency and impartiality of the Nigerian judicial system. He urged President Tinubu and the APC to recognise that Nigerians were closely monitoring developments within the country’s political landscape. He maintained that the survival of Nigeria’s democracy depended on protecting political plurality, strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring that voters, rather than institutional controversies, ultimately determined the country’s political leadership. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary_zh: 韩国和荷兰的科学技术主管部门周五在世宗特别自治市首次举行科学技术联合委员会会议，讨论了从投资计划到人工智能与科学研究政策等多项议题。韩国科学技术信息通信部表示，此次会议是在两国于2024年签署研究与科学合作谅解备忘录（MOU）之后举行的。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: Science ministries from Korea and the Netherlands held the first joint committee meeting on science and technology in the central city of Sejong on Friday and discussed a range of topics from investment plans to policy discussions on artificial intelligence and scientific research. The event came after a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on research and science cooperation was signed between the two countries in 2024, the Ministry of Science and ICT said. Research management agencies from the two countries agreed to build joint research models in areas of mutual interest, while the Korean side proposed strengthening ties in the field of quantum technology and synthetic biology, according to the ministry. "Building on the foundation of cooperation the two countries established in semiconductors, we were able to broaden the horizon to various advanced science technologies," the science ministry said, vowing to support future research collaboration between the two countries

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.title: Key lessons Korea should learn from US midterm elections
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.summary: Trump has been checked, not finished The U.S. midterm elections have delivered a decisive setback to President Donald Trump and the Republican Party. For Korea, the message is straightforward: Do not mistake a midterm election for the end of Trump or the Republican Party. The midterm elections demonstrate that American voters can hold their leaders accountable.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.summary_zh: 特朗普受挫，但尚未出局。美国中期选举给唐纳德·特朗普总统和共和党带来了决定性的挫折。对韩国而言，信息很明确：不要把中期选举误认为特朗普或共和党的末日。中期选举表明，美国选民能够追究其领导人的责任。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.body: Trump has been checked, not finished The U.S. midterm elections have delivered a decisive setback to President Donald Trump and the Republican Party. Democrats have captured both the House of Representatives and the Senate, fundamentally changing the political landscape in Washington. Yet the significance of this defeat should not be exaggerated. Trump has suffered a serious political setback, not a political death sentence. The Republican Party has lost control of Congress but remains a powerful political force. For Korea, misunderstanding this distinction could have serious consequences. Three issues contributed substantially to the Republican defeat: the war with Iran, concerns about corruption and the continuing struggle of ordinary Americans to afford everyday necessities. The Iran war has become a major political liability. However, dissatisfaction with the war should not automatically be interpreted as opposition to its strategic objectives. Some Americans recognize Iran as a serious security threat but question the administration's execution, costs and strategy for ending the conflict. Others oppose the war itself. As a former soldier, I believe military action must be judged not only by its justification but also by its objectives, execution and political consequences. Winning battles does not necessarily produce strategic success. Affordability has also influenced voters. Housing, food, energy, health care and declining purchasing power affect everyday life. Regardless of Washington's economic explanations, Americans judge their government by what they experience. Corruption represents another serious concern. Allegations involving conflicts of interest, personal enrichment and political favoritism have raised questions about accountability. Particularly troubling is the perceived scale, blatancy and apparent normalization of questionable conduct. Not every allegation constitutes proven wrongdoing, but the perception that political leaders operate under different rules is damaging. Nevertheless, Koreans should understand that Republican rejection does not mean Democratic endorsement. Many Americans voted against the administration's performance rather than out of renewed confidence in Democratic leadership. One encouraging development is that America's constitutional system continues to function. Trump has acknowledged the election results and indicated a willingness to work with Democrats, although confrontation is inevitable. His acceptance of the outcome is important, even if genuine cooperation remains uncertain. The incoming Democratic Congress will possess considerable investigative and legislative authority. Hearings, investigations, budget confrontations and challenges to executive decisions are likely. Impeachment may become part of the political debate, but removing a president requires a two-thirds Senate majority, making conviction difficult without substantial Republican support. Legislative stalemate appears more likely than dramatic political transformation. However, political deadlock does not necessarily mean democratic failure. America's constitutional system deliberately divides authority to prevent excessive concentrations of power. The coming confrontation will test whether political leaders respect those boundaries. How Washington conducts and concludes its Iran operations will provide important lessons for America's allies and adversaries alike. Iranian leaders may interpret the Democratic victory as evidence that Trump is politically finished and American pressure will diminish. That would be a dangerous miscalculation. Trump retains substantial presidential authority, particularly in foreign affairs and national security. Congressional opposition may complicate military policy, but it does not automatically prevent further action. Indeed, political setbacks sometimes encourage leaders to demonstrate resolve. This does not mean Trump will necessarily escalate the conflict. Nevertheless, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps could remain a potential American military target. Tehran should also recognize that American concerns about Iran extend beyond Trump and the Republican Party. Mistaking political division for strategic paralysis could prove costly. For Korea, the message is straightforward: Do not mistake a midterm election for the end of Trump or the Republican Party. Korean politicians, commentators and policymakers should resist the temptation to celebrate Republican losses or ridicule the U.S. president. Such behavior would be strategically shortsighted. More importantly, Koreans must remember that the U.S. is home to millions of decent, hardworking, patriotic citizens who are deeply proud of their country. They may disagree bitterly over politics, but their patriotism deserves respect. Criticizing a U.S. president is one thing. Insulting the American people is quite another. Koreans should also examine their own political shortcomings. Our country has experienced corruption, polarization, political scandals and abuses of power. We are hardly qualified to lecture Americans about the imperfections of democracy. There is a Korean proverb about a dog covered in filth criticizing another dog for having a little dirt on its coat. Americans have a similar expression: "People who live in glass houses should not throw stones." Before pointing fingers at Washington, Koreans should examine their own political conduct. We must also remember that these decent Americans are the people whose fathers, mothers, sons and daughters served, fought and died alongside Koreans defending our freedom. Their sacrifices deserve respect regardless of political affiliation. Temporary political disagreements must never become expressions of national arrogance or ingratitude. The Korea-U.S. alliance is not a relationship between one Korean administration and one U.S. political party. It is a partnership between two nations whose security and prosperity remain closely connected. Seoul must therefore maintain productive relationships with the Trump administration, Democratic congressional leaders and influential Republicans. This is especially important as both countries confront North Korea's nuclear threat, defense burden-sharing, wartime operational control transition and military modernization. Koreans are entitled to personal opinions about American politics. However, public officials and influential figures must distinguish between personal preferences and statements that could damage national interests. The midterm elections demonstrate that American voters can hold their leaders accountable. They also show that military decisions, economic hardship and concerns about government integrity carry electoral consequences. But America's political divisions have not disappeared. They have entered a new institutional environment. For Korea, the appropriate response is neither celebration nor alarm. It is strategic patience, diplomatic discipline, humility and respect for the American people. The Republican Party has been defeated, but it has not disappeared. Above all, Americans deserve our respect. Alliances must remain stronger than the political fortunes of individual leaders. In diplomacy, knowing when to keep one's opinions to oneself can be just as important as knowing what to say. Chun In-bum is the former commander of the Republic of Korea Army Special Warfare Command
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.title_zh: 韩国应从美国中期选举中汲取的重要经验
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.body_zh: 特朗普受挫，但尚未出局。美国中期选举给唐纳德·特朗普总统和共和党带来决定性挫折。民主党赢得了众议院和参议院的控制权，从根本上改变了华盛顿的政治格局。然而，不应夸大这次失败的意义。特朗普遭遇的是严重的政治挫折，而不是政治死刑。共和党失去了对国会的控制，但仍是强大的政治力量。对韩国而言，误解这一区别可能造成严重后果。三个问题促成了共和党的败选：与伊朗的战争、腐败问题，以及普通美国人继续难以负担日常生活必需品。对这场战争的不满，已成为一个重大政治负担。然而，不应自动把对战争的不满解读为反对其战略目标。一些美国人承认伊朗构成严重安全威胁，但质疑政府在结束冲突时的执行方式、成本和战略。另一些人则反对战争本身。作为一名前军人，我认为，军事行动不仅要以其理由是否正当来衡量，还要看其目标、执行方式和政治后果。赢得战斗并不一定能带来战略成功。可负担性也影响了选民的投票。住房、食品、能源、医疗保健和购买力下降都会影响日常生活。无论华盛顿如何解释经济状况，美国人都会根据自身经历来评判政府。腐败是另一个严重关切。涉及利益冲突、个人牟利和政治偏袒的指控，引发了人们对问责机制的质疑。尤其令人不安的是，这种不当行为的规模、公开程度，以及似乎已趋于正常化的状态，并非每项指控都能构成经证实的不法行为，但认为政治领导人遵守不同规则的观感会造成损害。尽管如此，韩国人应明白，共和党落选并不意味着民主党获得背书。许多美国人投票是为了反对本届政府的表现，而不是出于重新看好民主党领导层。一个令人鼓舞的进展是，美国的宪政体系仍在发挥作用。特朗普承认了选举结果，并表示愿意与民主党合作，尽管冲突不可避免。他接受选举结果十分重要，即便真正合作的前景仍不确定。即将上任的民主党国会将拥有相当大的调查和立法权。听证、调查、预算博弈以及对行政决定的挑战都很可能出现。弹劾可能成为政治辩论的一部分，但罢免总统需要参议院三分之二多数，因此在缺少大量共和党支持的情况下，很难定罪。立法僵局似乎比剧烈的政治转型更有可能出现。然而，政治僵局并不一定意味着民主失败。美国的宪政体系有意分权，以防止权力过度集中。即将到来的对抗将考验政治领导人是否尊重这些边界。华盛顿如何实施并结束对伊朗的行动，将为美国的盟友和对手 alike 提供重要启示。伊朗领导人可能把民主党的胜利解读为特朗普在政治上已经出局、美国施压将减弱的证据。那将是危险的误判。特朗普仍掌握相当大的总统权力，尤其是在外交事务和国家安全方面。国会的反对可能使军事政策复杂化，但不会自动阻止进一步行动。事实上，政治挫折有时会促使领导人展示决心。这并不意味着特朗普必然会升级冲突。尽管如此，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队仍可能成为美国潜在的军事目标。德黑兰也应认识到，美国对伊朗的关切不局限于特朗普和共和党。把政治分歧误判为战略瘫痪，可能会付出代价。对韩国而言，信息很明确：不要把中期选举误认为特朗普或共和党的末日。韩国政界人士、评论人士和政策制定者应抵制庆祝共和党败选或嘲笑美国总统的诱惑。这种做法在战略上是短视的。更重要的是，韩国人必须记住，美国是数百万正直、勤奋、爱国公民的家园，他们为自己的国家深感自豪。他们可能在政治问题上激烈分歧，但他们的爱国精神值得尊重。批评美国总统是一回事，侮辱美国人民则完全是另一回事。韩国人也应审视自身的政治缺陷。我们的国家经历过腐败、政治极化、政治丑闻和滥用权力。我们 hardly 有资格就民主的不完美来教训美国人。韩国有句谚语，说一条满身污泥的狗嘲笑另一条狗的外套上沾了一点土。美国也有类似的说法：“住在玻璃房子里的人不应扔石头。”在指责华盛顿之前，韩国人应先审视自己的政治行为。我们还必须记住，这些正直的美国人的父亲、母亲、儿子和女儿曾与韩国人并肩服役、战斗并牺牲，保卫我们的自由。无论政治立场如何，他们的牺牲都值得尊重。暂时的政治分歧绝不能变成民族傲慢或忘恩负义的表现。韓美同盟不是韩国一个政府与美国一个政党之间的关系，而是两个安全与繁荣紧密相连的国家之间的伙伴关系。因此，首尔必须与特朗普政府、民主党国会领导人以及有影响力的共和党人维持富有成效的关系。这一点尤其重要，因为两国都在应对朝鲜核威胁、防务负担分担、战时作战指挥权移交和军事现代化。韩国人可以对美国政治持个人意见。然而，公职人员和有影响力的人物必须区分个人偏好与可能损害国家利益的言论。中期选举表明，美国选民能够追究领导人的责任，也显示军事决策、经济困境和政府对廉洁的关切都会带来选举后果。但美国的政治分歧并未消失，而是进入了一种新的制度环境。对韩国而言，适当的回应既不是庆祝，也不是惊慌，而是战略耐心、外交纪律、谦逊和尊重美国人民。共和党已经败选，但并未消失。最重要的是，美国人民值得我们的尊重。联盟必须比个别领导人的政治命运更加牢固。在外交中，知道何时把意见留给自己，可能与知道该说什么同样重要。辛仁范是韩国陆军特战司令部前司令。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.title: Finance minister vows timely actions to ease stock market volatility
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.summary: The country's finance minister said Friday that the financial authorities will map out measures to help the local stock market be less volatile amid the ongoing tech rout. In an economy-related meeting, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said the U.S. midterm elections are an important watershed for the global economy, saying that overnight falls on Wall Street in the face of tighter regulations on AI-related sectors would deliver a blow to the global market.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.summary_zh: 该国财政部长周五表示，在科技股持续遭遇抛售之际，金融机构将制定措施，帮助本土股市降低波动。在一次 Economy 相关会议上，财政部长李炯逸表示，美国中期选举是全球经济的重要分水岭，并称，在人工智能相关行业监管收紧的情况下，华尔街隔夜下跌将冲击全球市场。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body: The country's finance minister said Friday that the financial authorities will map out measures to help the local stock market be less volatile amid the ongoing tech rout. In an economy-related meeting, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said the U.S. midterm elections are an important watershed for the global economy, saying that overnight falls on Wall Street in the face of tighter regulations on AI-related sectors would deliver a blow to the global market. Lee said the Korean economy's fundamentals are more solid than ever before and vowed to respond to external uncertainties. Shortly after the opening bell, trading of the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for 20 minutes, as the benchmark index plunged by more than 8 percent amid tech sell-offs

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.title: Tinubu has shown he cares about workers with ₦70,000 allowance
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.summary: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated concern for workers’ welfare through the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance. Oshiomhole made the statement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s performance and urged Nigerians to appreciate its policies.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.summary_zh: 代表埃多州北区的参议员亚当斯·奥肖莫霍勒表示，联邦政府批准每月发放₦70,000交通津贴，体现出总统博拉·蒂努布对劳动者福祉的关切。奥肖莫霍勒周四接受《Channels Television》的《今日政治》节目采访时发表上述言论，并为蒂努布政府的施政表现辩护，同时敦促尼日利亚人珍惜政府的各项政策。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.body: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated concern for workers’ welfare through the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance. Oshiomhole made the statement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s performance and urged Nigerians to appreciate its policies. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” he said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, insisting that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. Oshiomhole also criticised the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which Atiku Abubakar served as vice-president, alleging that it failed to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. He said the 2027 presidential election would offer Nigerians a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whom he accused of allowing multiple exchange rates that favoured people based on their connections. The senator also faulted the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, for allegedly failing to present an alternative to Tinubu’s policies. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” Oshiomhole said. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.title_zh: 蒂努布以₦70,000津贴表明自己关心工人
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.body_zh: 代表埃多州北区的参议员亚当斯·奥希奥莫霍尔表示，联邦政府批准每月向劳动者发放₦70,000交通补贴，说明总统博拉·蒂努布切实关注劳动者福祉。奥希奥莫霍尔周四在Channels Television的《今日政治》节目中接受采访时作出上述表态。他为蒂努布政府的表现辩护，并敦促尼日利亚民众 appreciate 其政策。他说：“我认为本届政府表现良好。如果一个人原本领取₦70,000，如今又获得₦70,000，那么他的收入就是₦140,000，增幅达到100%。如果你明白₦10,000对普通民众意味着什么，你就会体会到蒂努布确实表示了关切。”联邦政府在10月27日与尼日利亚劳工大会（NLC）会晤后，批准从2026年11月起，为各级劳动者提供为期六个月的每月₦70,000交通补贴。协议还规定，从11月开始，分三个月的等额 installments 支付拖欠的特殊津贴。然而，尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）拒绝接受交通补贴方案，坚持认为劳动者需要永久性加薪，而不是临时救济。奥希奥莫霍尔还批评了奥卢塞贡·奥巴桑乔前总统执政时期，指出阿蒂库·阿布巴卡尔曾任该政府副总统，并声称政府未能确保按时支付劳动者工资。他说，2027年总统选举将让尼日利亚民众在蒂努布和阿蒂库之间作出选择；他认为蒂努布实现了统一汇率，而阿蒂库则纵容多种汇率并存，使有关系的人从中受益。这位参议员还指责尼日利亚民主党（NDC）总统候选人彼得·奥比，称其未能提出取代蒂努布政策的替代方案。奥希奥莫霍尔说：“彼得·奥比没有提出任何替代方案。我一直说彼得·奥比是个商人；商人的逻辑是短期周转。蒂努布所代表的是政治家式的思维，他会考虑下一代。”奥希奥莫霍尔说。本文所表达的观点不代表Vanguard newspapers及其任何员工的意见

https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.title: From The Strait Of Hormuz To The Strait Of Midterm, Trump Pays Heavy Price
https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.summary: The midterm results just re-echoed Stoken’s point that the pendulum of US politics swings toward the middle all the time, not despite the voters, but because of them. But because the Democratic Party had lost its way by creating a nanny state, compounding red tape, and deifying wokeism, Trump’s idiosyncrasies looked like middle ground. It remains to be seen if, finally, the midterm has taught the Trump White House the lesson that it failed to learn from turning the world on its head.
https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.summary_zh: 中期选举结果再次印证了斯托肯的观点：美国政治的钟摆始终朝向中间路线，不是因为选民而偏离中间路线，而是正因为选民才会如此。然而，由于民主党通过建立保姆型国家、层层增加繁文缛节并将 wokeism 奉为圭臬而迷失方向，特朗普的特立独行看起来便像是中间路线。仍待观察的是，中期选举是否终于让特朗普白宫吸取教训，而这一教训它此前在试图颠覆世界时未能学会。
https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.body: The midterm results just re-echoed Stoken’s point that the pendulum of US politics swings toward the middle all the time, not despite the voters, but because of them. One Trump term (2017-2021) was enough. But because the Democratic Party had lost its way by creating a nanny state, compounding red tape, and deifying wokeism, Trump’s idiosyncrasies looked like middle ground. He was voted in again in 2024, despite his hubris. Two years later, the pendulum is swinging left again. It’s funny that a president who dragged the US into a needless Middle East war with serious economic consequences for the world, sparked global tariff wars, criminalised migration, and bullied neighbours and allies alike is unable to save his party from electoral ruin. Voters have just reminded him that all 45 presidents who have occupied the White House since 1776 are tenants, not owner-occupiers. If it were up to him, Trump would have stuffed the ballots, created a crisis, or manufactured any subterfuge to change the results. But despite his disdain for process, his vindictive narrow-mindedness and desperation for vengeance, he could not. Despairing voters tamed him on November 3. Americans, or at least a significant number of them, have delivered the first nationwide verdict on Trump’s second term. Midterms are not a presidential election, but this one almost assumed the character of one – with President Barack Obama and Trump himself hitting the road and mounting the soapbox. The outcome is a Democratic breakthrough that feels like a landslide. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives were on the ballot, along with 35 of the 100 Senate seats and 36 governorships. The stakes were straightforward: Republicans controlled both chambers of Congress. Following the polls, Democrats flipped the hitherto red Congress to blue. The contest itself was not merely between two parties. It was between two versions of America – one energised by Trump’s MAGA delusions; the other alarmed by the cost of living, Trump’s misuse and abuse of power, and the slow unravelling of the American dream. As an unwritten rule, midterm elections often punish the president’s party. Voters, having handed a president the keys to the White House, return two years later to endorse or denounce the state of affairs. And since Trump-2 happened, the state of affairs has been not just perilous but life-threatening. With Americans being shot on the streets by ICE agents in what is clearly state-sanctioned murder, and vindictive attacks on critics like Ilhan Omar, the election assumed unusual urgency. Trump himself led the Republican campaigns, asking voters to assume he was on the ballot. That was a clear indication that, despite his incorrigibility, he was troubled by a likely unfavourable verdict – which is what he got. He told Americans to pretend he was on the ballot (he recanted after the devastating defeat), and offered a generous $5,000 bribe for every vote if Republicans won. His oligarch, Elon Musk, reportedly spent $474 million. Yet, Trump was punished, and Republicans lost. His approval rating has been near record lows, with public dissatisfaction focused on the economy and a foolish war in Iran, which a Republican Congress never felt any urgency about but felt helpless to stop. The election results are proof that Trump has been a liability and a political misadventure at the White House, as Republican candidates struggled to distance themselves from a president who demands loyalty and rarely admits error. They were still Trump enablers, and their loss should not be mourned. For Democrats, the election has been a breath of fresh air, and an opportunity to rebuild and regain institutional leverage. Theirs is broader than opposition to Trump. They campaigned on affordability – housing, prices, healthcare, and energy – while presenting themselves as the party prepared to check executive excesses. Their challenge was to turn anger into a governing argument, not merely a protest vote. The parties were not evenly matched in mood. Polling and early voting data indicated strong Democratic enthusiasm. Compared with Republicans, Democrats seemed far more motivated to vote, a sign that opposition to Trump brought infrequent voters to the polls – something party leaders had not succeeded at. Moreover, Trump’s claims on the economy, as with every other claim, became contested territory. Bloomberg reported that his handling of the economy, alongside the war in Iran, contributed to his very low approval ratings. Immigration was another defining issue. For Trump’s base, border enforcement is a promise kept. For Democrats and many independents, the obvious fact is that enforcement has become murderous, indiscriminate, divisive and damaging to America’s image. For young, minority and urban voters, immigration is a moral and civil-rights question. Foreign policy was another layer. The war in Iran has turned national security from a Republican talking point into a subject of scrutiny. Voters may support a strong military, but they also ask what a war would cost, who would fight it, and whether it would make everyday life safer. Americans showed up even with protest votes. Early voting data showed that roughly 54 million Americans had already cast ballots before election day. Of those, about 43 per cent were Democrats, 32 per cent were Republicans, and 25 per cent were independents or unaffiliated voters. More striking is the reported increase in turnout among voters of colour in the states that release race and ethnicity data. That matters because Democrats made gains among young, non-white and previously disengaged voters – groups that traditionally turn out at lower rates in midterms. The election was not decided in California or New York, where outcomes are largely predictable. It was decided in a handful of competitive states and districts: North Carolina, Georgia, Maine, Michigan, Texas, Ohio and Alaska were among the key battlegrounds. Now with Democrats in control of Congress, Trump’s final two years could change. For example, the Democratic Congress can investigate administration decisions, subpoena officials, scrutinise spending, examine the conduct of the war in Iran, and challenge policies on immigration, healthcare and the economy. The days of a rubber-stamp Congress may be well and truly over, and tougher scrutiny may be expected. Yet, while winning Congress gives Democrats substantial power to investigate, block new legislation and bargain over funding, it does not necessarily give them the votes to dismantle Trump’s existing legislative programmes while he remains president. Controversial Trump-signed laws, such as the tax-and-spending law in 2025 (the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill), the mandatory immigration detention for certain non-citizens charged with specified offences (the Laken Riley Act 2025), and federal judicial appointments, will be harder to reverse than imagined. Underestimate a demagogue at your peril. Trump may well rule America for the rest of his term by veto and Executive Orders, without Congress. It remains to be seen if, finally, the midterm has taught the Trump White House the lesson that it failed to learn from turning the world on its head. The pendulum is swinging back to the middle, but it’s still early days to be excited. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.title_zh: 从霍尔木兹海峡到中期选举海峡，特朗普付出沉重代价
https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.body_zh: 中期选举结果再次印证了斯托肯的观点：美国政治的钟摆始终在向中间摆动，这并非违背选民的意愿，而是因为选民才使它如此。特朗普的一届任期（2017—2021年）已经足以说明问题。但民主党通过打造保姆国家、层层叠加繁文缛节并将 wokenism 奉为圭臬而迷失方向后，特朗普的特立独行反倒显得像是中间路线。尽管他傲慢自负，他仍在2024年再次当选。两年后，钟摆又开始向左摆动。颇有意思的是，这位把美国拖入一场毫无必要的中东战争、给世界经济造成严重后果，挑起全球关税战，将移民刑事化，并欺凌邻国和盟国的总统，竟无法挽救自己的政党免遭选举惨败。选民刚刚提醒他，自1776年以来入主白宫的45位总统都是房客，而不是自有自住的业主。如果由他做主，特朗普会往选票箱里塞东西、制造危机，或编造任何花招来改变结果。然而，尽管他蔑视程序、心怀报复且狭隘偏执、急于雪耻，最终还是无法得逞。11月3日，绝望的选民制服了他。美国人，或者至少相当一部分美国人，已经就特朗普第二任期作出首次全国性裁决。中期选举并非总统选举，但这一次几乎具有总统选举的性质——总统巴拉克·奥巴马和特朗普本人亲自巡回各州站台造势。结果是一场民主党大突破，颇似压倒性胜利。众议院全部435个席位、参议院100个席位中的35席以及36个州长职位均接受选举。利害关系很简单：共和党此前控制国会两院。计票结束后，民主党把原本属于共和党的国会翻转为蓝色。这场较量不只是两党之间的竞争，也是两个版本的美国之间的较量——一个被特朗普的“MAGA”迷思所激励，另一个则对生活成本、特朗普滥用和滥用权力，以及美国梦缓慢瓦解深感不安。按照一条不成文的规则，中期选举往往会惩罚总统所属政党。选民把白宫钥匙交给总统后，两年后便会回来肯定或谴责现状。自特朗普第二任期开启以来，局势不仅危险，更攸关生死。美国人在街头被美国移民与海关执法局（ICE）特工枪击，这显然是国家纵容的谋杀；对伊尔汗·奥马尔等批评者的报复性攻击也令此次选举具有异乎寻常的紧迫性。特朗普亲自领衔共和党的竞选活动，要求选民假定他本人也在选票上。这清楚表明，尽管他桀骜难驯，却因可能遭受不利裁决而不安——而他确实遭遇了这一裁决。他告诉美国人假装自己就在选票上（遭遇惨败后他改口否认），并承诺若共和党获胜，每张选票将获得慷慨的5,000美元贿赂。据报道，他的寡头盟友埃隆·马斯克投入了4.74亿美元。然而，特朗普仍受到惩罚，共和党败选。他的支持率接近历史低点，公众的不满集中于经济以及在伊朗打的那场愚蠢战争。共和党国会从未觉得有紧迫感去处理这场战争，却又束手无策地无法阻止。选举结果证明，特朗普一直是白宫的负担和一次政治误判，因为共和党候选人竭力与这位要求忠诚、极少认错的总统划清界限。他们仍是特朗普的帮凶，他们的失败不值得哀悼。对民主党而言，这次选举令人耳目一新，也提供了重建并重获制度影响力的机会。民主党的立场远不只是反对特朗普。他们围绕生活可负担性展开竞选——住房、物价、医疗和能源——同时把自己塑造成准备制衡行政权力越界的政党。他们面临的挑战，是把愤怒转化为治国理据，而不只是投一张抗议票。两党的情绪基础并不同等。民调和提前投票数据显示，民主党热情高涨。与共和党相比，民主党选民似乎更有投票动力，这表明反对特朗普促使那些不常投票的人走进投票站，而这是党内领导人此前未能做到的。此外，特朗普对经济的说法，和他的其他所有说法一样，也成为争议地带。彭博社报道称，他对经济的处理以及伊朗战争共同导致了他的支持率极低。移民是另一个决定性议题。对特朗普的基本盘而言，边境执法是已经兑现的承诺。对民主党和许多独立选民而言，显而易见的事实是，执法已经变得杀戮化、缺乏选择性、具有分裂性，并损害了美国形象。对年轻选民、少数族裔选民和城市选民而言，移民是道德和公民权利问题。外交政策是另一层因素。伊朗战争已把国家安全从共和党的宣传口号变成受审视的议题。选民或许支持强大的军队，但也会追问战争要付出什么代价、谁来参战，以及它能否让日常生活更安全。美国人即使投的是抗议票，也出来投票了。提前投票数据显示，约有5,400万美国人在选举日之前已经投票。其中，约43%是民主党人，32%是共和党人，25%是独立选民或无党派选民。更引人注目的是，据报道，在公布种族和族裔数据的州，有色人种选民的投票率有所上升。这一点很重要，因为民主党在年轻选民、非白人选民和此前政治疏离选民中取得了进展，而这些群体在中选举中的传统投票率较低。决定此次选举胜负的并非结果大体可预测的加利福尼亚州或纽约州，而是少数竞争激烈的州和选区：北卡罗来纳州、佐治亚州、缅因州、密歇根州、得克萨斯州、俄亥俄州和阿拉斯加州均属关键战场。如今民主党掌控国会，特朗普最后两年的处境可能会改变。例如，民主党国会可以调查政府的决策、传唤官员、审查开支、检查伊朗战争的行为，并挑战移民、医疗和经济方面的政策。橡皮图章式国会的日子或许真的结束了，更严格的监督可以预期。然而，赢得国会虽然赋予民主党相当大的权力，可以展开调查、阻止新立法并围绕拨款进行谈判，却不一定会让他们在特朗普仍是总统时获得足够的票数来推翻他现有的立法计划。由特朗普签署的争议性法律，例如2025年的税收与支出法（所谓《一项宏大而美好的法案》）、对被控犯有特定罪行的某些非公民实行强制拘留的《莱肯·赖利法案2025》，以及联邦司法任命，推翻难度将超出人们的想象。低估煽动者必然后悔。特朗普完全可能凭借否决权和行政命令，在没有国会的情况下继续主导美国余下的任期。中期选举是否终于教会了特朗普白宫从把世界掀翻这件事中未能吸取的教训，仍有待观察。钟摆正在摆回中间，但现在还远不到兴奋的时候。我们占了上风。获取实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角，直接送达你的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入 https://dailytrust.com/muslim-candidates.body: Muslim candidates made history in Tuesday’s US midterm elections, winning seats in Congress and state legislatures despite a campaign marked by a surge in anti-Muslim rhetoric and attacks targeting their communities. The results included the election of America’s first Muslim senator, an Egyptian-American surgeon who treated wounded Palestinians in Gaza, and several Palestinian-American candidates. The victories came after President Donald Trump and his allies targeted Muslim candidates, particularly Michigan’s Abdul El-Sayed, who faced baseless allegations linking him to extremist groups. At least seven Muslim candidates were elected to Congress, including one senator and six House representatives. Egyptian-American Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan to become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. A physician and public health specialist, El-Sayed campaigned on healthcare, living costs and reducing corporate influence in politics. He also criticised US military assistance to Israel and Egypt, while rejecting accusations of Muslim Brotherhood links made by political opponents. Egyptian-American surgeon Adam Hamawy defeated Republican Greg Mele in New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District, becoming the state’s first Muslim representative in Congress. A former US Army surgeon, Hamawy helped save the life of future senator Tammy Duckworth after her helicopter was shot down in Iraq in 2004. He later volunteered in Gaza, treating Palestinians wounded in Israeli attacks, including children with severe injuries. Rashida Tlaib: Palestinian-American congresswoman wins again Rashida Tlaib secured a fifth term representing Michigan’s 12th Congressional District. The Palestinian-American Democrat, one of the first two Muslim women elected to Congress in 2018, remains a prominent critic of Israel’s war on Gaza. The Somali-American Democrat, another of Congress’s first Muslim women, has repeatedly criticised US support for Israel and faced attacks from President Donald Trump. Darializa Avila Chevalier: First Latina Muslim congresswoman The 33-year-old Democrat, of Dominican heritage, was reported to have become the first Latina Muslim woman elected to Congress. She previously gained prominence through civil rights activism and pro-Palestinian protests. Two other Muslim Democrats secured re-election to the House. Andre Carson retained Indiana’s 7th District, which he has represented since 2008, while civil rights advocate Lateefah Simon won another term in California’s 12th District. Her family was displaced from Palestine in 1948, eventually settling in the United States. Kawas campaigned on affordable housing, healthcare, immigrant rights and opposition to US funding for Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. Lebanese-American Democrat Abbas Alawieh was elected to Michigan’s 2nd State Senate District, covering Dearborn and surrounding communities. Alawieh helped establish the Uncommitted movement, which challenged former President Joe Biden’s support for Israel during the 2024 presidential election. Previously a state representative, Syed’s victory transferred the seat from Republican to Democratic control. Arab-American Republican Darin LaHood retained his Illinois congressional seat. LaHood, whose great-grandparents emigrated from Lebanon, has spoken proudly of his Lebanese heritage, saying: “I’m very proud of that heritage.” He also co-chairs the US-Lebanon Friendship Caucus and has worked to strengthen ties between Washington and Beirut. Several Palestinian-American candidates also secured victories in state legislative elections, including Iman Jodeh in Colorado’s 29th State Senate District and Ruwa Romman in Georgia’s 7th State Senate District. In Illinois, Palestinian-American Democrat Abdelnasser Rashid was projected to retain his state House seat. Other Muslim women reportedly elected included Zaynab Mohamed in Minnesota, Munira Abdullahi in Ohio, Maryam Khan in Connecticut and Madinah Wilson-Anton in Delaware. https://dailytrust.com/muslim-candidates.body_zh: 穆斯林候选人在周二的美国中期选举中创造了历史。尽管此次竞选充斥着反穆斯林言论激增以及针对其社区的袭击，他们仍在国会和州议会赢得了席位。选举结果包括美国首位穆斯林参议员的诞生，他是一名曾在加沙治疗受伤巴勒斯坦人的埃及裔美国外科医生，以及多名巴勒斯坦裔美国候选人的胜选。此前，总统唐纳德·特朗普及其盟友针对穆斯林候选人展开攻击，尤其是密歇根州的阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德，后者遭到毫无根据的指控，被声称与极端组织有关。至少有7名穆斯林候选人当选国会议员，其中包括1名参议员和6名众议员。42岁的埃及裔美国民主党人阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德在密歇根州击败共和党人迈克·罗杰斯，成为首位当选美国参议员的穆斯林。作为一名医生和公共卫生专家，埃尔-赛义德以医疗保健、生活成本以及减少企业影响政治为竞选主题。他还批评美国对以色列和埃及的军事援助，同时驳斥政治对手关于其与穆斯林兄弟会有关联的指控。埃及裔美国外科医生亚当·哈马维在新泽西州第12国会选区击败共和党人格雷格·梅莱，成为该州首位进入国会的穆斯林代表。作为一名前美国陆军外科医生，2004年未来参议员塔米·达科沃斯的直升机在伊拉克遭击落后，哈马维曾协助挽救她的生命。此后，他自愿前往加沙，治疗在以色列袭击中受伤的巴勒斯坦人，其中包括遭受严重伤害的儿童。拉希达·特莱布：巴勒斯坦裔美国女议员再次胜选拉希达·特莱布成功赢得第五个任期，继续代表密歇根州第12国会选区。这位巴勒斯坦裔美国民主党人是2018年首批当选国会的两名穆斯林女性之一，她仍是加沙战争的主要批评者。这名索马里裔美国民主党人是国会首批穆斯林女性之一，曾多次批评美国对以色列的支持，并遭到总统唐纳德·特朗普的攻击。达里亚利萨·阿维拉·谢瓦利耶：首位拉丁裔穆斯林女议员据报道，这名33岁的民主党人拥有多米尼加裔背景，成为首位当选国会的拉丁裔穆斯林女性。她此前因参与民权行动和声援巴勒斯坦示威而广受关注。另有两名穆斯林民主党人成功赢得众议员连任。安德烈·卡森守住了印第安纳州第7选区，他自2008年以来一直代表该选区；民权活动家Lateefah Simon则在加利福尼亚州第12选区再次赢得一个任期。她的家人在1948年被迫离开巴勒斯坦，后来最终在美国定居。卡瓦斯以可负担住房、医疗保健、移民权利以及反对美国资助以色列在加沙实施的种族灭绝战争为竞选主题。黎巴嫩裔美国民主党人阿巴斯·阿拉维赫当选密歇根州第2州参议院选区议员，该选区覆盖迪尔伯恩及周边社区。阿拉维赫曾协助建立“不承诺”运动，在2024年总统选举期间挑战前总统乔·拜登对以色列的支持。阿拉维赫此前担任州众议员，赛义德的胜选使该席位由共和党掌控转为民主党掌控。阿拉伯裔美国共和党人达林·拉胡德守住了他在伊利诺伊州的国会席位。拉胡德的曾祖父母来自黎巴嫩，他曾自豪地谈及自己的黎巴嫩血统，并表示：“我为这份血统深感自豪。”他还共同主持美国—黎巴嫩友好小组，并努力加强华盛顿与贝鲁特之间的联系。数名巴勒斯坦裔美国候选人也在州议会选举中获胜，包括科罗拉多州第29州参议院选区的伊曼·乔德和佐治亚州第7州参议院选区的鲁瓦·罗曼。在伊利诺伊州，巴勒斯坦裔美国民主党人阿卜杜勒-纳赛尔·拉希德预计将保住其州众议员席位。据报道，其他当选的穆斯林女性还包括明尼苏达州的泽纳布·穆罕默德、俄亥俄州的穆妮拉·阿卜杜拉希、康涅狄格州的玛丽亚姆·汗，以及特拉华州的马迪娜·威尔逊-安东尼。巴基斯坦裔美国议员萨尔曼·博贾尼和苏莱曼·拉拉尼也在得克萨斯州成功连任；绍德·阿马尔守住了康涅狄格州参议院席位，塔里克·汗则在宾夕法尼亚州众议院再次赢得一个任期。加入《每日信任》WhatsApp社群，快速获取身边新闻与动态

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: SEATTLE — Democrats' sweeping victories in Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections brought relief to many Koreans frustrated with President Donald Trump, but that relief did not necessarily translate into support for the Democratic Party. That was how Bo Young Lee, a Korean American business executive, summed up the election results. "Ultimately, the results on Tuesday were a byproduct of citizens' frustration with the Trump administration, rising costs, and the attacks on democracy," Lee, an international speaker specializing in AI ethics and corporate diversity, told The Korea Times. Another Korean American voter, a 47-year-old Texas resident who has traditionally supported Republicans, said she crossed party lines for the first time in Tuesday's election. "I voted Democratic simply because I wanted anyone but the Republicans," she said, requesting anonymity. "It was the first time in my life I'd ever voted for a Democrat." Her decision came as Texas, long considered a Republican stronghold, delivered some of the election's biggest surprises. Democrats won the governorship and a U.S. Senate seat in the state for the first time in decades, marking a dramatic shift in a state that had consistently rejected Democratic candidates in statewide races. The Democratic victories dealt a major setback to Trump, giving the party control of both chambers of Congress and setting the stage for a divided government during the remaining two years of his presidency. Across Korean-language online communities, the results prompted everything from celebrations to expressions of disbelief and cautious optimism. "I've lived in the U.S. for 20 years, and this is the first time I've paid so much attention to a midterm election," one commenter wrote. "I thought America had no hope after Trump became president for a second time. Now I feel a little reassured. At least there will be some checks on Trump's unchecked power." Another commenter said the results brought tears, describing the comfort of realizing that many others shared the same frustrations. Yet the conversations also showed that opposition to Trump did not necessarily translate into support for Democrats. One California resident said they had traditionally voted Republican because of disagreements with Democratic policies but voted Democratic this time out of frustration with Trump. "I absolutely despise Trump, but I don't support Democrats either because I disagree with many of their policies," one person wrote. Much of the debate centered on everyday concerns rather than party loyalty. Some blamed Trump's tariffs and economic policies for worsening the cost of living. Others worried that Democratic policies would increase government spending and place greater burdens on middle-class families. Education also emerged as a contentious issue, particularly among parents discussing LGBTQ-related topics in schools. Some expressed concerns about what their children were being taught, while others pushed back against what they considered exaggerated fears. The contrasting views highlighted differing political views among Korean Americans, with some putting aside longstanding party loyalties to oppose Trump while others remained skeptical of Democratic policies. Lee said the results reflected broader dissatisfaction with the Trump administration, but warned that Democrats should not take their victories for granted. "The newly elected Democrats can't forget the frustration that swept them into office. If people don't see meaningful change within a short period, we may see different results in 2028," she said
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 旅美韩国人欢迎民主党取得胜利，但对未来走向仍存疑虑
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 西雅图——民主党在周二举行的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，这让许多对唐纳德·特朗普总统感到失望的韩国人如释重负，但这种宽慰未必转化为对民主党的支持。旅美韩裔企业高管Bo Young Lee正是这样总结此次选举结果的。李在接受《韩国时报》采访时说：“归根结底，周二的结果是公民对特朗普政府的不满、生活成本上涨以及针对民主制度的攻击共同造成的副产品。”李是一名专注于人工智能伦理和企业多元化的国际演讲者。另一名旅美韩裔选民是一名47岁的得克萨斯州居民，过去一直支持共和党；她说，周二这次选举是她首次跨党派投票。“我投票给民主党，只是因为除了共和党之外，我愿意支持任何人。”她表示，并要求匿名。“这是我有生以来第一次投票给民主党人。”她的决定出现在得克萨斯州出人意料的选举结果之中。长期以来，得克萨斯州一直被视为共和党的大本营，但在此次选举中，民主党数十年来首次赢得该州州长职位和一个美国联邦参议院席位，这在该州全州范围的选举中历来拒绝民主党候选人的背景下，标志着一场剧烈转变。民主党的胜利对特朗普构成重大打击，使该党掌控了国会两院，并为特朗普剩余两年任期内的分立政府局面铺路。在韩语网络社群中，选举结果引发了庆祝、难以置信和谨慎乐观等不同反应。一名评论者写道：“我在美国生活了20年，这是第一次如此关注中期选举。我原以为特朗普第二任期开始后，美国就毫无希望了。现在我感到稍微安心了一些。至少会对特朗普不受制约的权力形成一些制衡。”另一名评论者说，选举结果令她感动落泪，因为意识到许多人也怀着同样的不满。然而，讨论也表明，反特朗普并不一定会转化为支持民主党。一名加利福尼亚州居民说，由于与民主党政策存在分歧，他过去一直投票给共和党，但此次出于对特朗普的不满而投票给民主党。一人写道：“我非常厌恶特朗普，但也不支持民主党，因为他们许多政策都与我相左。”争论大多围绕日常生活问题，而非党派忠诚。一些人将生活成本恶化归咎于特朗普的关税和经济政策。另一些人担心，民主党的政策会增加政府支出，给中产家庭带来更沉重的负担。教育也成为一个有争议的话题，尤其是在讨论学校 LGBTQ相关议题的家长之中。一些人担忧孩子正在接受的教育内容，另一些人则反驳他们认为被夸大的恐惧。这些对立观点凸显了韩裔美国人之间不同的政治立场：一些人搁置长期以来的党派忠诚，以反对特朗普；另一些人则仍对民主党政策持怀疑态度。李表示，选举结果反映了人们对特朗普政府更广泛的不满，但警告民主党不应把胜利视为理所当然。她说：“新当选的民主党人不能忘记，正是这股不满情绪把他们推上了台。如果人们短期内看不到有意义的改变，那么2028年我们可能会看到不同的结果。”

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 纽约——周四，与人工智能数据中心建设相关的股票再次遭遇大幅下挫，跌幅压倒华尔街，并抹去了该指数前一天的全部涨幅，而前一天是其三个月来表现最好的一天。自唐纳德·特朗普总统于2025年4月宣布“解放日”关税、震动全球市场以来，华尔街正有望录得自那以来的最严重跌幅。人工智能芯片股是华尔街最具影响力的股票类别之一，因为其中一些已经成为规模最大的股票。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: NEW YORK — Another wipeout for stocks tied to the buildout of AI data centers is overwhelming Wall Street on Thursday and more than erasing all its gains from the day before, which was its best in three months. The S&P 500 fell 3.2 percent after opening with a loss that accelerated through the morning. It’s on track for its worst drop since President Donald Trump shook markets worldwide in April 2025 after announcing his “Liberation Day” tariffs. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 1,146 points, or 2.1 percent, as of 11 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 5 percent lower. Stock markets worldwide felt pressure from continued drops for companies that benefited from the boom for the artificial-intelligence technology industry, and South Korea’s Kospi index tumbled 5.3 percent. Such stocks have been swinging for months on worries that the construction of further AI data centers may slow because of how expensive it’s become to borrow money . Nvidia fell 8.3 percent and was by far the heaviest weight on the S&P 500, a day after dropping 3.2 percent. Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 15.9 percent. CoreWeave, a company that rents access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, fell 14.9 percent. GE Vernova, which has been helping to power data centers, sank 9.1 percent. AI chip stocks are some of Wall Street’s most influential because they’ve become some of the largest. A 1 percent move for Nvidia, for example, has more effect on the S&P 500 than a 1 percent move for nearly any other U.S. stock. Leading them was AppLovin, which soared 30.2 percent after the marketing platform reported both revenue and profit that topped analysts’ expectations. It also approved a program to send up to $3.2 billion to its investors by buying back its own stock, bringing the program’s total potential value to $3.6 billion. Tapestry rallied 6.7 percent after the company behind the Coach and Kate Spade brands likewise delivered a stronger profit than expected. It also raised its forecasts for revenue and earnings this fiscal year. Stock prices tend to follow where corporate profits and interest rates go over the long term, depending on them much more than on who controls what in Washington. In other financial markets, the initial knee-jerk reaction to the U.S. midterm election results faded a bit. The price of a barrel of Brent crude oil rose 2.2 percent to $96.70 and recovered a chunk of its nearly 9 percent drop from the day before. Uncertainty still reigns about what will happen in the war with Iran and when the global energy industry can return to normal. In the bond market, Treasury yields continued to ease. The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.84 percent from 4.90 percent late Wednesday. It had been at 4.95 percent on election night and above 5.30 percent last month. That could be a signal that investors are herding into U.S. Treasury bonds in search of something that’s safer to own than stocks. The drop also came despite some encouraging reports on the U.S. economy. Fewer U.S. workers applied for unemployment benefits last week. A separate report, meanwhile, suggested overall productivity for U.S. workers improved by more during the summer than economists expected. That could help the economy grow without adding pressure to the nation’s high inflation. In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed in Europe and Asia. Besides South Korea, Japan’s Nikkei 225 also felt the sting of drops for tech and AI-related stocks and sank 1.8 percent. London’s FTSE 100 dipped 0.1 percent after the Bank of England increased its main interest rate for the first time in three years to help limit high inflation. The bank said its next moves on interest rates largely hinge on what happens with the Iran war , which sent oil prices and inflation higher worldwide. “We’ve seen encouraging news in the past 48 hours,” Bank Gov. Andrew Bailey said at a press briefing. “The best thing that can happen is to resolve the conflict in the Middle East; there’s no question about it.”
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 人工智能芯片股下挫，华尔街或迎来2025年特朗普宣布关税以来最糟糕的一天
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 纽约——周四，与人工智能数据中心建设相关的股票再次遭遇重挫，令华尔街承压，并抹去了前一日的全部涨幅，而前一日是该指数三个月以来的最佳表现。标普500指数低开3.2%，跌幅在上午进一步扩大，按目前走势将创自美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于2025年4月宣布“解放日”关税并震动全球市场以来的最大单日跌幅。截至美东时间上午11时，道琼斯工业平均指数下跌1,146点，跌幅为2.1%；纳斯达克综合指数下跌5%。在全球股票市场，受人工智能技术产业繁荣带动而受益的公司持续下跌，各市场均承受压力，韩国综合股价指数重挫5.3%。数月来，这类股票一直大幅波动，市场担忧，随着借贷成本变得十分昂贵，进一步建设人工智能数据中心的步伐可能放缓。Nvidia下跌8.3%，成为拖累标普500指数的最主要因素；此前一日，该股已下跌3.2%。Advanced Micro Devices重挫15.9%。CoreWeave通过云端向客户提供人工智能芯片使用服务，其股价下跌14.9%。为数据中心供电的GE Vernova暴跌9.1%。人工智能芯片股是华尔街影响力最大的股票之一，因为它们已成为市值最大的股票之一。例如，Nvidia股价每变动1%，对标普500指数的影响都超过美国其他几乎任何一只股票变动1%带来的影响。AppLovin领涨，在营销平台公布的营收和利润均超过分析师预期后，股价飙升30.2%。该平台还批准了一项最高向投资者支付32亿美元的股票回购计划，使该计划潜在总价值达到36亿美元。Tapestry上涨6.7%，此前这家Coach和Kate Spade品牌背后的公司同样公布了高于预期的利润，并上调了本财年的营收和盈利预测。长期来看，股票价格往往取决于企业利润和利率的走向，相比华盛顿由谁掌控，对这些因素的关注程度要高得多。在其他金融市场，美国中期选举结果公布后的初步本能反应已有所消退。每桶布伦特原油价格上涨2.2%，至96.70美元，收复了前一日近9%跌幅中的很大一部分。围绕对伊战争将如何发展以及全球能源行业何时能够恢复正常，不确定性仍然占据主导地位。在债券市场，美国国债收益率继续回落。10年期美国国债收益率从周三晚间的4.90%降至4.84%。选举之夜该收益率为4.95%，上月则高于5.30%。这或许表明，投资者正涌入美国国债，以寻找比股票更安全的持有资产。此次股市下跌还伴随着美国经济方面的一些鼓舞人心 reports。上周申请失业救济的美国工人减少。与此同时，另一份报告显示，美国劳动者的整体生产率在夏季的改善幅度超过经济学家预期。这可能有助于经济增长，同时不会给该国的高通胀带来额外压力。在海外股票市场，欧洲和亚洲各指数表现不一。除韩国外，日本日经225指数也受到科技和人工智能相关股票下跌的冲击，下跌1.8%。英格兰银行三年来首次提高主要利率，以帮助抑制高通胀，伦敦金融时报100指数随后下跌0.1%。该行表示，其下一步利率行动将在很大程度上取决于伊朗战争的发展，而这场战争已推高全球油价和通胀水平。英格兰银行行长Andrew Bailey在新闻发布会上说：“过去48小时，我们看到了一些令人鼓舞的消息。最好的结果是解决中东冲突；这一点毫无疑问。”

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: WASHINGTON — Korean American Rep. Dave Min (D-CA) of the U.S. Democratic Party won reelection to the U.S. House of Representatives, securing a second term in Congress, according to a race projection. The AP has called the race for Min over Republican Jenny Rae Le Roux in California's 47th congressional district as vote counting continued following Tuesday's midterm elections. With 62 percent of the vote counted, Min had secured 56.9 percent, leading Le Roux by 13.8 percentage points. Min, 50, was born in Rhode Island in 1976 to Korean immigrant parents. He graduated from the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard Law School before working as an enforcement attorney at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. He later taught law at the University of California, Irvine, before entering politics. Min first ran for Congress in 2018 but finished third in the Democratic primary. He later won a seat in the California State Senate in 2020 and worked on legislation involving gun control and environmental protection. He made a successful second bid for the U.S. House in 2024, narrowly defeating Republican Scott Baugh in California's 47th district. Min became the third Korean American candidate win a congressional race in Tuesday's midterms, following Rep. Marilyn Strickland (D-WA) and Democratic Rep.-elect Dan Koh of Massachusetts. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 韩裔美国众议员戴夫·明赢得美国众议院连任选举
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 华盛顿——据选举结果预测，美国民主党韩裔众议员戴夫·明（加州选区）成功连任美国众议院议员，将在国会获得第二个任期。周二中期选举后计票仍在进行之际，美联社已判定明在加利福尼亚州第47选区击败共和党人珍妮·雷·勒鲁克斯。已统计62%的选票时，明获得56.9%的支持率，领先勒鲁克斯13.8个百分点。50岁的明于1976年出生于罗得岛州，父母均为韩国移民。他毕业于宾夕法尼亚大学和哈佛法学院，之后曾在美国证券交易委员会担任执法律师，后来在加州大学尔湾分校教授法律，随后进入政界。明于2018年首次竞选国会议员，但在民主党初选中名列第三。2020年，他赢得加利福尼亚州参议院席位，并参与推动涉及枪支管控和环境保护的立法。2024年，他再次竞选美国众议员并成功连任，在加利福尼亚州第47选区以微弱优势击败共和党人斯科特·博。继华盛顿州众议员玛丽莲·斯特里克兰和马萨诸塞州候任民主党众议员丹·科之后，明成为周二中期选举中第三位赢得国会选举的韩裔美国候选人。斯特里克兰赢得第四个任期，科则成为当选美国国会议员的第七位韩裔美国人

https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/k.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription The INDIA bloc on Thursday adopted a five-point resolution at its “Save the Vote, Save the Nation” protest at Freedom Park, demanding the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the rejection of the revised electoral rolls in Karnataka. The declaration also urged the State government to conduct the forthcoming local body, taluk and zilla panchayat elections using the pre-SIR 2025 electoral rolls. It called for the repeal of the law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and the restoration of an independent selection process in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directions. The resolution alleged that the names of more than 14 crore voters had been removed from electoral rolls nationwide. In Karnataka, the electorate had declined from 5.54 crore to approximately 4.5 crore in the final list published on October 27. Of the 99.32 lakh names removed, approximately 23 lakh pertained to deceased and duplicate voters, while nearly 76 lakh were alleged to be eligible voters, including migrants and those who had shifted residence. In Bengaluru, the number of voters has fallen from 1.04 crore to 59.08 lakh, with nearly 45 lakh names deleted, the declaration stated. It questioned the deletion of migrant voters and alleged that instead of updating their addresses through Form 8, they were being asked to apply afresh through Form 6. The resolution also alleged misuse of Form 7 applications by BJP workers to seek deletion of voters’ names and questioned the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) handling of such complaints. Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced that the State government would initiate a police investigation into the alleged misuse of Form 7 applications. “There is CCTV footage showing who instigated vote theft and who brought the applications. Cases will be registered in this regard, and justice will be delivered,” he said. He alleged that Form 7 applications had been printed at the BJP office and circulated among constituency-level leaders along with voters’ names and identification details. He appealed to Booth Level Officers (BLOs) to cooperate in exposing the alleged irregularities. “Our principal demand is that the names of all voters deleted from the electoral rolls, except those who are deceased, must be restored,” he said, adding that the agitation would continue until justice was delivered to affected voters. Mr. Siddaramaiah said the large-scale reduction in Karnataka’s electorate raised serious concerns about the voting rights of eligible citizens. He demanded that the ECI disclose the reasons for the deletions and ensure that no eligible voter was excluded without due process. Questioning the changes to the selection process for election commissioners, he said the replacement of the Chief Justice of India with a Union Minister in the selection committee had raised concerns about the Election Commission’s independence. Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee president B.K. Hariprasad said the protest was a continuation of the nationwide agitation held at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1 under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge. “All political parties that believe in constitutional values and democratic institutions must unite,” he said. INDIA联盟周四在自由公园举行的“拯救选票，拯救国家”集会上通过了一项五点决议，要求取消选民名册特别集中修订（SIR）、首席选举专员Gyanesh Kumar辞职，并拒绝承认卡纳塔克邦修订后的选民名册。

声明还要求邦政府使用SIR实施前的2025年选民名册，举行即将到来的地方机构、塔卢克和县议会选举。决议呼吁废除有关首席选举专员任命的法律，并依照最高法院的指示恢复独立遴选程序。

决议称，全国范围内有超过1400万选民的姓名被从选民名册中删除。在卡纳塔克邦，最终名单于10月27日公布后，选民人数从5540万降至约450万。在被删除的993.2万个姓名中，约23万个属于已故选民和重复登记者，另有近76万个据称是符合条件的选民，包括外来务工人员和已经搬迁住所者。

声明称，在班加罗尔，选民人数从1040万降至590.8万，近450万个姓名被删除。声明质疑删除外来务工选民的合理性，并称他们本应通过第8号表格更新地址，却被要求通过第6号表格重新申请。

决议还称，BJP工作人员滥用第7号表格申请，以要求删除选民的姓名，并质疑印度选举委员会（ECI）对此类投诉的处理方式。

首席部长D.K. Shivakumar在集会上宣布，邦政府将就是否滥用第7号表格申请启动警方调查。他说：“有监控录像显示是谁煽动窃取选票、是谁提交了这些申请。我们将就此立案，并会伸张正义。”

他称，第7号表格申请是在BJP办公室打印的，并连同选民姓名和身份信息分发给各选区负责人。他呼吁投票站级官员（BLOs）配合揭露涉嫌违法不当的行为。

他说：“我们的主要要求是，除已故选民外，所有从选民名册中删除的选民姓名都必须恢复。”他补充说，在正义得到伸张、受影响选民的权益得到保障之前，抗议活动将持续进行。

Siddaramaiah先生表示，卡纳塔克邦选民人数大幅减少，引发了对符合资格的公民投票权的严重关切。他要求ECI公开删除选民姓名的原因，并确保任何符合条件的选民都不会在未经正当程序的情况下被排除在选民名册之外。

他质疑对选举专员遴选程序的改动，称在遴选委员会中由一名联邦部长取代印度首席大法官，引发了对选举委员会独立性的担忧。

卡纳塔克邦国大党委员会主席B.K. Hariprasad表示，这次抗议是11月1日在新德里Ramlila Maidan举行的全国性抗议活动的延续，该活动由Rahul Gandhi和Mallikarjun Kharge领导。

他说：“所有信奉宪法价值和民主制度的政党都必须团结起来。”他补充说，INDIA联盟将加强在卡纳塔克邦各地区的行动。

https://leadership.ng/agric-minister-to-.body: The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Abubakar Kyari is expected to lead other stakeholders at the opening of the 2026 National Agricultural Show scheduled to hold in November. The five-day event, organised by the National Agricultural Foundation of Nigeria (NAFN), will take place at the national agricultural showground in Nasarawa State. Kyari will attend as the special guest of Honour6 at the opening ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. In a statement, NAFN national coordinator, Aishatu Rufa’I Ibrahim, called on federal and state governments, local government authorities, private-sector operators, financial institutions, development partners and farmers to participate actively in the agricultural gathering. She said the annual show remained a major national platform for showcasing agricultural innovations, technologies, products, investment opportunities and practical solutions to challenges confronting Nigeria’s agricultural and food systems. According to her, this year’s edition is particularly important amid growing concerns over food security, rising production costs, climate change, limited access to finance, inadequate mechanisation and the need to strengthen agricultural value chains. She said the event would provide opportunities for stakeholders to exchange knowledge, establish strategic partnerships, explore investment opportunities and promote policies capable of transforming the agricultural sector. The NAFN coordinator urged federal and state ministries, departments and agencies , local government areas, organised private-sector organisations, financial institutions, research institutions, agribusiness investors, farmers’ associations, cooperatives, smallholder and commercial farmers to take advantage of the programme. She said government institutions would have opportunities to showcase their agricultural programmes, attract partnerships and identify practical interventions to advance rural development and food security. Ibrahim added that private-sector participants would benefit from networking, market access, business-to-business engagements and opportunities to invest across different agricultural value chains. For farmers, particularly smallholder producers, she said the show would provide exposure to improved technologies, modern farming practices, quality agricultural inputs, market linkages and opportunities to connect directly with service providers and potential buyers. The foundation said the show was designed to move stakeholders beyond discussions to practical collaborations and measurable outcomes that would strengthen Nigeria’s agrifood system. She said, “The annual national agricultural show remains a premier national platform for showcasing agricultural innovations, technologies, products, investment opportunities and practical solutions to the challenges confronting Nigeria’s agricultural and food systems. This year’s edition is particularly significant against the backdrop of growing concerns over food security, rising production costs, climate change, limited access to finance, inadequate mechanization and the need to strengthen agricultural value chains. “It will provide an opportunity for stakeholders to exchange knowledge, establish strategic partnerships, explore investment opportunities and promote policies that will transform Nigeria’s agricultural sector. NAFN believes that achieving sustainable food security requires collective action, strong public-private partnerships, increased investment and the adoption of innovative agricultural solutions. https://leadership.ng/agric-minister-to-.body_zh: 尼日利亚农业与粮食安全部长阿布巴卡·基亚里预计将率其他利益相关方为2026年全国农业展揭幕，展览定于11月举行。这场为期五天的活动由尼日利亚国家农业基金会（NAFN）组织，将在纳萨拉瓦州国家农业展览场举行。基亚里将于11月17日星期二作为尊贵嘉宾出席开幕式。NAFN全国协调员艾莎图·鲁法伊·易卜拉欣在一份声明中呼吁联邦和州政府、地方政府当局、私营部门运营商、金融机构、发展伙伴及农民积极参与本次农业盛会。她说，年度展览仍是展示农业创新、技术、产品、投资机会以及应对尼日利亚农业和粮食体系所面临挑战的切实解决方案的重要全国平台。据她介绍，在人们日益关注粮食安全、生产成本上升、气候变化、融资渠道有限、机械化不足以及加强农业价值链需求的情况下，今年的展览尤其重要。她说，本次活动将为各利益相关方提供交流知识、建立战略伙伴关系、探索投资机会以及推动能够改变农业部门面貌的政策的机会。NAFN协调员敦促联邦和州各部委、司局和机构、地方政府辖区、有组织的私营部门组织、金融机构、研究机构、农业企业投资者、农民协会、合作社、小规模农户和商业农户充分利用本次项目。她说，政府机构将有机会展示其农业项目、吸引合作伙伴，并确定推进农村发展和粮食安全的切实干预措施。易卜拉欣补充称，私营部门参与者将从建立人脉、进入市场、企业对业务接洽以及投资不同农业价值链的机会中受益。对于农民，尤其是小规模生产者，她说，展览将使其接触改良技术、现代耕作方式、优质农业投入品、市场连接渠道，以及与服务提供商和潜在买家直接建立联系的机会。基金会表示，展览旨在推动各利益相关方超越讨论，开展切实合作并取得可衡量的成果，以加强尼日利亚的农业食品体系。她说：“全国年度农业展仍是展示农业创新、技术、产品、投资机会以及应对尼日利亚农业和粮食体系所面临挑战的切实解决方案的首要全国平台。在人们日益关注粮食安全、生产成本上升、气候变化、融资渠道有限、机械化不足以及加强农业价值链需求的情况下，今年的展览格外重要。“本次活动将为各利益相关方提供交流知识、建立战略伙伴关系、探索投资机会以及推动能够改变尼日利亚农业部门面貌的政策的机会。NAFN认为，实现可持续粮食安全需要集体行动、强有力的公私伙伴关系、加大投资以及采用创新农业解决方案。全国农业展为所有利益相关方提供了超越讨论、开展切实合作并取得可衡量成果的独特机会。我们掌握独家优势。订阅LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，即可在手机上直接获取实时报道、独家内幕和独家视角。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS，通过WhatsApp获取全天候最新动态 →

https://www.inquirer.net/494789/naga-cit.body: Comelec spokesperson John Rex Laudiangco said voter registration in Naga City would be temporarily suspended due to the November 21 plebiscite on its proposed conversion into a highly urbanized city. READ: Comelec to reopen voter registration on Nov. 10 for 2028 polls Meanwhile, Laudiangco said voter registration in six municipalities in Batanes would not reopen on November 10 due to the special elections scheduled on November 28 to fill a vacant seat in the House of Representatives. The six municipalities are Basco, Itbayat, Ivana, Mahatao, Sabtang, and Uyugan. Batanes lone district Rep. Ciriaco Gato Jr. died on September 21 due to cardiac arrest, leaving the congressional seat vacant. Laudiangco said registration would proceed in the rest of the country until July 30, 2027. READ: Comelec receives 4.7-M voter registration applications The Comelec will also bring its Special Register Anywhere Program to malls, airports, terminals, call centers, and universities to make voter registration more accessible. “Sa SRAP [Special Register Anywhere Program], doon magparehistro. Kami na po ang bahalang mag-publish ng pangalan ninyo, mag-aayos ng status ninyo at sisiguraduhin po namin, kung qualified po kayo, magiging registered voter kayo,” Laudiangco said. (Register through the SRAP. We will take care of publishing your name, updating your registration status and ensuring that you become a registered voter if you are qualified.) He also said that the poll body currently has around 69 million registered voters and expects the number to increase by 3 million during the eight-month registration period, bringing the total to between 71 million and 72 million. The figure differs from the 71 million registered voters earlier cited by Comelec Chairperson George Erwin Garcia in October. The poll body is also preparing to offer online reactivation services for voters whose registration records have been deactivated for failing to vote in two consecutive elections. Under the online reactivation system, applicants may access the application form through the Comelec’s iRehistro portal, fill in their personal information and generate a PDF copy of the application. The accomplished and signed form must then be submitted through email. Laudiangco also said the Comelec would schedule a video conference with applicants to verify their identities before deciding whether to approve their reactivation. “Magsasagawa lamang po tayo ng isang parang video conferencing. Magpapadala kayo via email ng form. At pag masiguro namin through the video conferencing na kayo nga ‘yan, eh yun na po yun,” he said. (We will simply conduct a video conference. You will send the form through email. Once we are able to verify through the video conference that you are indeed the applicant, that will be it.) Voters who have transferred to another residence may also apply for reactivation and transfer of registration at the same time using one form. Your subscription could not be saved. Please try again. Your subscription has been successful. Laudiangco clarified that voters who failed to participate in only one election would not yet be deactivated. Katherine Cielo Guimera/INQUIRER.net trainee /jpv
https://www.inquirer.net/494789/naga-cit.title_zh: Naga City和Batanes的6个城镇将不在11月10日重新开放选民登记
https://www.inquirer.net/494789/naga-cit.body_zh: 菲律宾选举委员会发言人约翰·雷克斯·劳迪扬科表示，由于纳加市拟于11月21日就是否升格为高度城市化城市举行公民投票，当地选民登记将暂时暂停。阅读：菲律宾选举委员会将于11月10日重新开放选民登记，为2028年选举做准备。与此同时，劳迪扬科说，巴坦群岛六个市镇的选民登记不会在11月10日恢复，因为当地定于11月28日举行特别选举，以填补众议院的一个空缺席位。这六个市镇是巴斯科、伊特巴亚特、伊瓦纳、马哈塔奥、萨布唐和乌尤甘。巴坦群岛唯一选区众议员小西里亚科·加托于9月21日因心脏骤停去世，留下国会议席空缺。劳迪扬科说，全国其他地区的登记将持续至2027年7月30日。阅读：菲律宾选举委员会收到470万份选民登记申请。菲律宾选举委员会还将把“随处特别登记计划”带到商场、机场、客运站、呼叫中心和大学，以便选民更容易完成登记。劳迪扬科说：“在SRAP〔随处特别登记计划〕下，你们可以登记。我们会负责公布你们的姓名、更新你们的登记状态，并确保你们如果符合条件，就成为已登记选民。”（通过SRAP完成登记。我们将负责公布你的姓名、更新你的登记状态，并确保你如符合条件，便成为已登记选民。）他还说，选举机构目前约有6900万名已登记选民，预计在八个月登记期内增加300万人，使总数达到7100万至7200万之间。这一数字与菲律宾选举委员会主席乔治·埃尔温·加西亚10月早些时候提到的7100万名已登记选民有所不同。选举机构还在准备提供选民重新激活在线服务，供那些因连续两次选举未投票而导致登记记录被停用的选民使用。在在线重新激活系统中，申请人可通过菲律宾选举委员会的iRehistro门户访问申请表，填写个人信息并生成PDF版申请表。填妥并签署的表格随后必须通过电子邮件提交。劳迪扬科还表示，菲律宾选举委员会将与申请人安排视频会议，以核实其身份，再决定是否批准重新激活。他说：“我们只会进行一次类似视频会议的沟通。你们通过电子邮件发送表格。等我们通过视频会议确认确实是你们本人申请后，这项程序就完成了。”已迁居其他住所的选民也可使用同一份表格，同时申请恢复登记和转移登记。您的订阅无法保存，请重试。您的订阅已成功。劳迪扬科澄清，仅有一次选举未投票的选民尚未被停用登记。Katherine Cielo Guimera/INQUIRER.net实习生 /jpv

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.summary: Time for Trump to transform his leadership The results of the U.S. midterm elections arrived earlier than expected here in Korea, and with a definitive outcome. As The New York Times wrote, "The system has held." Trump should heed the message his constituents have sent. South Korea must prepare for the possibility that Trump may bypass Seoul to engage with Pyongyang for his own political gain.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.summary_zh: 是时候让特朗普改变其领导方式了。美国中期选举结果比预期更早传回韩国，而且结果明确。正如《纽约时报》所言：“这个制度经受住了考验。”特朗普应当从选民传递的信息中汲取教训。韩国必须为特朗普可能绕过首尔，直接与平壤接触以谋取自身政治利益的可能性做好准备。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.body: Time for Trump to transform his leadership The results of the U.S. midterm elections arrived earlier than expected here in Korea, and with a definitive outcome. The Democrats won control of Congress, seizing both the House and the Senate. The forecast for a "blue wave" changed to a "blue tsunami" in a matter of hours, according to U.S. reports, as voters signaled they wanted change. The Democrats' victory was widely viewed as a repudiation of U.S. President Donald Trump's nearly two years in office. South Koreans closely watched the race for the Senate, where the decisive powers to check presidential powers lay. Democratic candidates even won Senate races in the traditionally Republican states of Texas, Kansas and North and South Carolina. Media reports showed the electorate voting for change as they worried about the state of democracy and the economy, as rising prices stemming from Trump's war on Iran decreased the quality of life for the average U.S. constituent. An AP poll also found that most voters were concerned about government corruption, signaling a "strong desire for Congress to take a more forceful role in checking the presidency." Democrats will now have the authority to do so. Here in South Korea, the issues that drove the U.S. electorate to vote for change serve as a refreshing reminder that democratic values still matter . A nation that has long been identified with its political system and values seems like it's back. As The New York Times wrote, "The system has held." Trump should heed the message his constituents have sent. The American president initially said he accepted the election results, congratulating the Democrats for "doing a good job" and blaming Republican candidates for inadequate campaigning. Trump later posted on social media an image of a red cap with the word "veto," hinting that he would exercise his veto powers on the opposition-controlled Congress. It would be difficult to find another U.S. midterm election that allied nations watched as closely as this one. The second Trump administration has pursued some unprecedented policies in trade and foreign affairs. His aggressive tariffs on both allies and non-allies compelled Korea to pledge $350 billion in investments in the U.S. in exchange for a flat rate tariff of 15 percent. On security and foreign affairs, Trump has expressed his frustration at the scale of U.S. military deployment to South Korea, which he has repeatedly criticized for not participating in the Iran war as he had requested. Trump also reduced joint military drills this summer. He continues to maintain openness toward North Korea and its leader Kim Jong-un, providing a chance for dialogue as Pyongyang refuses to engage with Seoul. South Korea must prepare for the possibility that Trump may bypass Seoul to engage with Pyongyang for his own political gain. The election outcome is prompting concerns that Trump will expand his existing trade and diplomatic policies, putting allies on edge. While the Lee Jae Myung administration does not expect major changes in relations with the U.S. following the midterm elections, South Korea should still be vigilant in the last two years of Trump's presidency. Trump's remaining years in office will likely be an uphill battle as Democrats flex their powers of check and balance. The Democrats' cautious approach to artificial intelligence and data centers could weigh on Korea's semiconductor industry and chip rally. Their prudent stance on nuclear nonproliferation may also bode negatively for Seoul's nuclear submarine ambitions. Trump earlier said he approved South Korea's request to build a nuclear-powered submarine, following a summit last year between the two leaders in Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province. The transfer of wartime operational control may also run into challenges as Democrats generally uphold the traditional alliance. U.S. allies, including Korea, will have to prepare for heightened uncertainty from a frustrated president facing new limitations as the opposition party regains control of Congress. Korea should prepare with these factors in mind
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.title_zh: Trump必须 heed 美国选民传递的信息
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.body_zh: 是时候让特朗普改变领导方式了。美国中期选举的结果比韩国媒体原先预计的更早出炉，而且结果明确。据美国媒体报道，数小时内，“蓝色浪潮”的预测就变成了“蓝色海啸”，选民表达了要求变革的意愿。民主党赢得国会控制权，同时拿下众议院和参议院。民主党在传统共和党占优的得克萨斯州、堪萨斯州以及北卡罗来纳州和南卡罗来纳州，甚至赢得了参议院选举。民主党在近两年执政期间受到广泛批评，被视为对特朗普总统执政表现的反证。韩国密切关注参议院选举，因为制衡总统权力的关键力量掌握在参议院。媒体报道显示，选民因担忧民主制度和经济状况而投票支持变革。特朗普对伊朗发动战争导致物价上涨，降低了普通美国公民的生活质量。美联社的一项民意调查还发现，多数选民担忧政府腐败，这表明选民“强烈希望国会采取更有力的行动制衡总统”。民主党如今将有权采取这种行动。在韩国，推动美国选民投票支持变革的种种问题令人耳目一新地提醒人们，民主价值观依然重要。这个长期以政治制度和价值观为民族特征的国家，似乎又找回了自身的方向。《纽约时报》写道：“这个制度经受住了考验。”特朗普应当从选民传递的信息中汲取教训。特朗普总统起初表示接受选举结果，祝贺民主党“干得不错”，并把竞选不力归咎于共和党候选人。后来，他在社交媒体上发布了一顶印有“否决权”字样的红色帽子，暗示他将对由反对党掌控的国会行使否决权。很难再找到另一场让盟国如此密切关注的美国中期选举。特朗普第二届政府推行了贸易和外交领域的一些前所未有政策。他对盟友和非盟友都加征强硬关税，迫使韩国承诺向美国投资3500亿美元，以换取15%的统一关税率。在安全和外交事务上，特朗普对美军在韩国的部署规模表示不满；他多次批评韩国没有按照他的要求参加对伊朗的战争。特朗普还削减了今年夏季的联合军演规模。他仍对朝鲜及其领导人金正恩持开放态度，在平壤拒绝与首尔接触的情况下，为对话提供了机会。韩国必须做好准备，因为特朗普可能绕开首尔，直接与平壤接触，以谋取自身政治利益。选举结果引发担忧，人们担心特朗普会扩大其现有贸易和外交政策，令盟国感到不安。尽管李在明政府预计中期选举后韩美关系不会发生重大变化，但在特朗普任期最后两年，韩国仍应保持警惕。随着民主党开始行使制衡权力，特朗普剩余的执政岁月很可能将是一场艰难鏖战。民主党对人工智能和数据中心持谨慎态度，可能对韩国半导体产业和芯片行情造成压力。他们在核不扩散问题上的审慎立场，也可能对首尔寻求核潜艇的努力产生不利影响。特朗普此前表示，在去年两位领导人于庆尚北道庆州举行峰会后，他已批准韩国建造核动力潜艇的请求。战时作战指挥权移交也可能遭遇挑战，因为民主党总体上支持传统盟国关系。包括韩国在内的美国盟国将不得不做好准备，应对一位因反对党重新掌控国会而面临新限制、并心怀不满的总统所带来的更大不确定性。韩国应考虑这些因素做好准备

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body: Cheong Wa Dae said Thursday it does not expect the results of the U.S. midterm elections to affect bilateral alliance, vowing to continue efforts to further develop the decadeslong alliance. "The Korea-U.S. alliance is one that has developed solidly over more than 70 years based on bipartisan U.S. support, and the results of certain elections are unlikely to affect the alliance," presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung told a press briefing following a meeting presided by President Lee Jae Myung. Kang said the Korean government would closely communicate and cooperate with both the U.S. administration and Congress to pursue the development of the alliance, while monitoring any changes in the political landscape. Kang, however, said the U.S. midterm elections were not discussed during Thursday's meeting. She added that Seoul will continue to pursue investment projects in the U.S. based on its agreement with the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump, noting the specifics of the investment would be reviewed under the principles of "national interests first," commercial reasonableness and relevant procedures. When asked whether the results could affect negotiations on the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) or nuclear-powered submarines in a YTN radio interview, she stressed that security agreements are based on mutual trust and are commitments that will be firmly upheld by both countries. Prime Minister Han Seong-sook also said she anticipates no big changes in relations with the U.S. after Trump's Republican Party suffered a crushing defeat. "As both the Democratic and Republican parties have considered the alliance between the two countries important, I think there will not be very big changes in relations with South Korea," Han said during a parliamentary budget committee meeting after a lawmaker asked her to assess the election results. She said the Democratic Party's victory was stronger than expected. "There are parts that we should analyze one by one in detail and other parts that require additional measures," Han said when asked about Seoul's diplomatic strategy toward Washington, adding that each relevant ministry is currently reviewing such issues
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.title_zh: 郑晚大：中期选举结果不太可能影响韩美同盟
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body_zh: 韩国总统府青瓦台周四表示，预计美国中期选举结果不会影响韩美同盟，并承诺继续努力推动已延续数十年的同盟关系进一步发展。总统发言人姜有璟在总统李在明主持的会议后举行的新闻发布会上说：“韩美同盟建立在美国两党支持的基础上，70多年来发展稳固，某些选举的结果不太可能影响这一同盟。”姜表示，韩国政府将与美国政府和国会保持密切沟通与合作，推动同盟关系发展，同时关注政治格局可能发生的变化。不过，姜指出，周四的会议并未讨论美国中期选举。她补充称，根据与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普政府的协议，首尔将继续推动对美投资项目，并指出，投资的具体事项将依据“国家利益优先”、商业合理性及相关程序原则进行审查。在YTN电台采访中，当被问及选举结果是否会影响战时作战指挥权移交或核动力潜艇方面的谈判时，她强调，安全协议建立在相互信任的基础上，是两国都会坚定履行的承诺。总理韩升洙也表示，预计特朗普所属共和党遭遇惨败后，美韩关系不会发生重大变化。韩在议会预算委员会会议上说：“由于民主党和共和党都重视两国之间的同盟关系，我认为与韩国的关系不会发生很大变化。”此前，一名议员请她评估选举结果。她说，民主党的胜利强于预期。在被问及首尔对华盛顿的外交策略时，韩表示：“有些方面需要逐一详细分析，另一些方面则需要采取额外措施。”她补充说，目前各相关部委正在审查这些问题
